newsitem.title: UK: GKN up on U.S. lawsuit damages hopes.
newsitem.headline: GKN up on U.S. lawsuit damages hopes.

text.p: Shares in GKN Plc were up 22p to 957-1/2p by 0835 GMT after the engineering group said late on Thursday that possible damages from a lawsuit brought by its U.S. franchising operation could fall by 30 percent or more.
"The news is a bit of relief more than anything else," said Harry Philips, analyst at Panmure Gordon.
GKN's U.S. franchisees first filed a case against GKN in December 1993, citing allegations that included breach of contract related to advertising payments.
In early February, lawyers for the franchisees said GKN could face damages of $740 million depending on the court's decision.
But on Thursday, GKN said a U.S. court had issued a notice on its likely decision in the case.

"Our preliminary assessment of the effect of this notice, if it is reflected in the judgement, is that the level of damages which might otherwise have been awarded against the various defendants would be reduced by 30 percent or more," GKN said.
Philips noted even the worst-case scenario of $740 million damages would not affect GKN's dividends for 1996, nor do any lasting damage to the company's prospects.
"This lawsuit issue, although important, should really have no bearing on whether to buy or sell the stock," Philips said.
"We take the view that the GKN balance sheet is more than strong enough to withstand even the worst case."
